version.changelog: 首次发布：支持有限次数重复的定时任务，自动在第N次执行后清理

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose, but it makes implementation assumptions (undeclared binary dependency and that task 'messages' will be executed as CLI commands) that could cause surprising behavior or leakage.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name and description (create a repeating task that auto-deletes after N runs) match what the script does: it calls the platform CLI to create a main repeating job and a one-shot deletion job. However the packaged metadata lists no required binaries while the script calls external tools (openclaw CLI and jq). The omission of jq/openclaw from required binaries is an inconsistency (likely an oversight) but not itself malicious.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The deletion job is created with its message set to the literal string "openclaw cron rm <main_id>" — the script assumes the platform will execute that message as a CLI command to remove the main job. If the platform does not execute message text as commands (instead delivering it as a chat message or to an external destination), the auto-delete will fail and the command text may be exposed to recipients. This is a behavioral assumption not documented in SKILL.md and could lead to surprising outcomes or information leakage.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + included script). Nothing is downloaded or extracted from external URLs, so there is no install-time network risk from the skill bundle itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials (good). It does, however, call external binaries (openclaw, jq, date) without declaring them. There are no requests for unrelated secrets or system paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request platform-wide persistent privileges. It operates by creating tasks via the openclaw CLI and does not modify other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Things to check before installing/use: 1) Ensure the openclaw CLI and jq are available in the runtime environment — the script uses `openclaw cron add` and `jq` but the skill metadata doesn't list them. 2) Confirm how your platform handles task "message" contents: this skill creates the deletion job by setting its message to the CLI command that removes the main job; if your platform only delivers messages to external channels (e.g., WeChat) instead of executing them, the auto-delete will not work and the command text may be sent to recipients. 3) Test in a safe channel and with small repeat counts (e.g., --repeat 2) to verify behavior before using on real targets. 4) Be aware that the deletion job will embed the main job ID in the message — consider whether leaking that ID or the raw command to the destination is acceptable. If you need, request the author to (a) declare required binaries (openclaw, jq) and (b) use an explicit deletion API call (or schedule a deletion job that runs an authenticated action) rather than relying on message execution.
